status: DRAFT nominal values for the unrecorded telemetry and acquisition electronics. Values documented for the equipment types used, not calibrations of the 1991 units.

preamp_zero_attenuation_gain_db.basis: McChesney (1999, USGS OFR 99-361): 'the USGS J502 has an unattenuated gain of 90 dB'; an 18 dB attenuator setting gives 72 dB. The Pinatubo VCO boards were CVO designs (T.L. Murray) on the J502 circuit (Lockhart et al., 1996), so the J502 value is assumed; the boards themselves were not measured. Lockhart's 'standard gain of 62-74 dB' for later CVO boards corresponds to 16-28 dB attenuation on this scale, consistent with the 18-36 dB settings of Appendix 1. The uncertainty is a judgement for an unmeasured custom board.

vco_hz_per_v.basis: McChesney (1999): 'The J502 and J512 produced by the USGS use 115 Hz / 4.05 V'.

discriminator_v_per_hz.basis: USGS J101 and J110 discriminators (Lockhart et al., 1996); their scale is not documented for Pinatubo. McChesney (1999) states that the VCO amplifier test-point signal has approximately the same amplitude as the discriminator output, i.e. discriminators matched to the 115 Hz / 4.05 V deviation; the inverse, 4.05 V / 115 Hz, is used, so VCO and discriminator together are 1 V/V.

adc_counts_per_v.basis: Data Translation DT2821 on WILLIE (Murray et al., 1996, citing Ellis, 1989): 12-bit, +/-10 V input range with programmable gains 1, 2, 4 and 8. The SUDS StationComp records of the archive give 'atod gain = 4' on seismic inputs, i.e. +/-2.5 V full scale: 4096 counts / 5 V. The DT2821 range and gain set are from the board's specification, not from a Pinatubo document.

omitted: Discriminator output filter and DT2821 anti-alias filter transfer functions are unknown and are not modelled; the passband is assumed flat at the 5 Hz reference frequency.
check: Lockhart et al. (1996): station gains were set so that ambient noise was 100 mV peak-to-peak at the VCO input; McChesney (1999) gives 50-100 mV as usual. With VCO and discriminator at 1 V/V and the ADC above that is 82 counts peak-to-peak. Step 70 compares this with the recorded pre-trigger noise in the first days of each documented epoch. The check tests the VCO-to-counts part of the chain, not the sensor or preamplifier gain.
